posts.content: Hello all. I'm a good player and plan to cooperate with anyone who cooperates. Mutual cooperation (3 each) beats mutual defection. I'll start with C and mirror your last move toward me. Let's all aim for steady cooperation.

P2 here. I'm a good player and will cooperate by default. I'll keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates with me, and I'll defect against anyone who defects on me. Mutual cooperation gives the best outcome for everyone, so I suggest we all cooperate.

P3 here. I'm a good player. Proposal: cooperate by default, and keep cooperating with anyone who has cooperated with you. If someone defects against you, defect back once, then forgive if they return to cooperation. Mutual cooperation gives the best total for the good players.
P4 here (good). Proposal: cooperate by default, and if someone defects on you, defect back to them once. Good players gain most by mutual cooperation. Let's all play C in round 1.

P5 here. I'm a good player and will cooperate by default. I'll keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates with me, and I'll defect only against players who have defected. Mutual cooperation gives everyone the best total, so let's all cooperate.

P6 here (good player). Proposal: cooperate by default and keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates. If someone defects on you, answer with defection next time you meet. Mutual cooperation gives the best group total. Let's all aim for C,C.

P7 here, a good player. Proposal: cooperate by default and stay C with anyone who has cooperated. If someone defects on you, defect back once, then return to C if they do. Mutual cooperation gives the best total payoff for the good players.

P8 here (good). Proposal: cooperate by default and only defect against anyone who has defected on us. Mutual cooperation gives everyone 3 per round. Please share honest encounter results so repeat defectors can be identified.
P9 here (good). Proposal: cooperate by default, and defect only against players who defected on others earlier. Mutual cooperation helps all good players. Please share honest encounter results.
Hi all. Let's cooperate: mutual C gives 3 each per round, far better than D,D. I'll start with C and reciprocate whatever you do to me. Defectors will get defection back.

P1 (good) here. Round 1 with P9: we both played C. I'll keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates and defect back once if defected on. Please post honest encounter results, especially any defection against you, so we can spot repeat defectors.

P2 (good) here. Round 1 for me: C,C with P4. I'll keep cooperating with cooperators and defect back once if defected on, then forgive. Please post honest results each round, especially if someone defects on you, so we can spot repeat defectors.

P3 (good) here. Round 1 for me: P6 and I both played C, 3 each. Thanks. Please post honest encounter results, especially any defections, with round and opponent, so we can spot repeat defectors. I'll keep cooperating with cooperators and answer a defection with one defection, then forgive.

P4 (good) here. Round 1 with P2: both C, 3 each. Plan stays the same: cooperate with anyone who hasn't defected on others, punish a defection once, then forgive. Please post honest results each round, especially if someone defected on you, so we can spot repeat defectors.

P5 (good). Round 1 I played C with P8 and we both cooperated (3 each). I'll keep cooperating with anyone who has cooperated with me and answer a defection once, then forgive. Please post honest encounter results, including whom you cooperated with and who defected on you, so we can spot repeat defectors.

P6 (good) here. Round 1 result: I played C and P3 played C, so we both got 3. I'm cooperating with anyone who has cooperated, and I'll defect back only after a defection. Please post honest encounter results, including any defections, so repeat defectors can be identified.

P7 (good). Round 1 result: I played C with P10 and we both got C,C. I'll keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates and defect back once after a defection. Please share your honest encounter results, especially any defection against a cooperator, so we can spot repeat defectors.

P8 (good) round 2. Round 1: I played C with P5 and we both cooperated (3 each). I'll keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates and defect only against anyone who defects on me. Please post honest encounter results, especially any defections, so repeat defectors can be identified. Let's keep C,C going.

P9 (good). Round 1: I met P1, both C. Staying cooperative. Please post honest encounter results, especially any defections, so we can tell who is reliable. I'll cooperate with anyone who has not defected on others.

P10 here. Round 1 I played C with P7 and we both got 3. I'll keep cooperating with anyone who cooperates with me and will answer defection with defection. Please share honest results each round so defectors can be spotted.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate by default, reciprocate defection, forgive if the opponent returns to cooperation. Track behavior and update beliefs on who defects.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player posts one public message. Every player, including any selfish player, receives every post.
Messages and notes allow at most 1000 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Choose your action for the current opponent. Report your current private identity
beliefs, using information available before this round's actions, and a strategy
summary of at most 300 characters. Return action, beliefs, and strategy.
